mechanism: NSAIDs may reduce the efficacy of levodopa by inhibiting renal prostaglandin synthesis and increasing sodium/fluid retention, while ketorolac also increases GI bleeding risk in patients taking levodopa; both drugs increase CNS effects and can elevate blood pressure.
action: Monitor blood pressure, levodopa efficacy, and signs of GI bleeding; consider alternative analgesic if possible; use lowest effective ketorolac dose for shortest duration.
